newsitem.title: USA: Tropical Storm Lili may become hurricane.
newsitem.headline: Tropical Storm Lili may become hurricane.

text.p: Tropical Storm Lili gained strength rapidly on Wednesday as it churned through the northwest Caribbean on a path toward western Cuba and southern Florida, the National Hurricane Centre said.
The storm, which grew out of a depression off the coast of Central America, gained tropical storm strength early on Wednesday and forecasters said it could be a hurricane by day's end.
Residents of western Cuba were put on hurricane alert and officials warned that heavy winds and rain could cause buildings to collapse in Havana.
In Florida, the government told residents to begin preparation for Lili's arrival as early as Friday.
At 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT), the centre of Lili was near latitude 18.6 north and longitude 84.0 west, or about 335 miles (535 km) south-southwest of Havana.
The storm was moving north-northwest at about 8 mph (13 kph). Maximum sustained winds were near 60 mph (95 kph) and were expected to strengthen during the next 24 hours.

The government of Cuba, which had previously issued a hurricane watch for the Isle of Youth and the western mainland provinces of Pinar del Rio and Havana, extended it to include the provinces of Matanzas, Villa Clara and Cienfuegos.

A tropical storm warning -- alerting residents to imminent storm conditions -- was in effect for the Cayman Islands and the east coast of Mexico's Yucatan peninsula from Cabo Catoche southward to Bahia de Chetumal, the hurricane centre said.

The hurricane centre also said a hurricane watch was likely to be issued for the Florida Keys later on Wednesday. Tropical Storm Lili would become a hurricane if its maximum sustained winds reached 74 mph (119 kph).
Florida authorities told residents to begin preparations for the storm -- which could reach the mainland by Friday -- by fuelling cars, securing homes and planning evacuation routes.

Cuban weather forecasters said the storm was likely to cross the western part of the island between Wednesday night and Thursday morning. Authorities advised citizens to clean up rubbish and in the countryside, farmers were told to take measures to help avoid flooding and protect animals.
In the city of Havana, the fire brigade warned that there could be house collapses. Bad weather has caused partial or total collapses of some 70 homes in poor and decaying conditions so far in 1996.

Cuba, slowly emerging from the worst of economic crisis caused by the collapse of the former Soviet Union, could be badly hit by a bad storm or hurricane. At this time of year, the key sugar cane crop, a crucial source of foreign exchange, is just two or thre months away from being harvested.
The western province of Pinar del Rio is where most of the island's tobacco crop is grown.
